title: Palmers Green & Winchmore Hill
intro: Edwardian suburbs built around two great parks, with a village green, a Quaker meeting house and some of the London Underground's finest stations nearby.

items.name: Grovelands Park
items.blurb: A landscaped park with a lake and woods around Grovelands House, a villa of 1797 by John Nash and Grade I listed.
items.tip: The lake and its woodland walk are the best part.

items.name: Broomfield Park
items.blurb: Palmers Green's park, with ornamental lakes, a conservatory, gardens and the shell of Broomfield House, a Tudor mansion damaged by fire.
items.tip: The conservatory is a sheltered spot on cold days.

items.name: Winchmore Hill Green
items.blurb: A village green with old houses, pubs and shops, and Church Hill rising beside it to an 18th-century Quaker meeting house.
items.tip: Walk up Church Hill for the prettiest houses.

items.name: Southgate station
items.blurb: A round 1933 station by Charles Holden, often compared to a flying saucer, Grade II* listed.
items.tip: Look at the bronze 'Tesla coil' on the roof.

items.name: Arnos Park and the viaduct
items.blurb: A long park following the Pymmes Brook, crossed by the brick viaduct of the Piccadilly line built in the 1930s.
items.tip: Follow the brook under the arches.
